function.name: calculate_velocity
function.description: Calculate the final velocity of an object in motion given its initial velocity, acceleration and time. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity of the object in m/s. This is a float type value.

acceleration.description: The acceleration of the object in m/s^2. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time for which the object is in motion in seconds. This is a float type value.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time data on the latest movie releases. However, you can check popular movie databases such as IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes, or your local cinema’s website for the most up‑to‑date information. If you’d like, I can help you find a specific genre or title that’s currently playing.
message.reasoning: User asks: "What are the latest movie releases?" We need to respond with a list of recent movies. But we don't have real-time data. We can provide a general answer or ask for clarification. According to policy, we should not hallucinate. So we should say we don't have up-to-date info. We can offer to search but no browsing. So we can say we can't provide current releases.
